comments: Input facts: ego and agent1 are cars; ego initiates and agent1 responds; both share a travel lane and direction. Chosen assumptions: ego approaches at 11-12 m/s while agent1 maintains 6-7 m/s 26-29 m ahead. Ego creates the conflict by maintaining its faster speed until separation is below 12-14 m, then waiting another 0.5-0.7 s before braking at 0.8-0.95 for 1.2-1.5 s and settling to agent1 speed. Agent1 responds by maintaining a predictable lane and speed. This is a delayed following-distance correction, rather than a throttle surge. The straight corridor and 8 s horizon are assumptions; collision is not required.
